title: A nowhere-dense closed subscheme of a one-dimensional scheme has dimension zero
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $\dim X\le 1$ [def-pc-dimension], and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subscheme (given by a closed immersion $Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]) whose underlying set is nowhere dense in $X$. Then $\dim Z\le0$ (with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$), and every point of $Z$ is closed in $Z$.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty then $Z$ is empty and the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise, the finite-type morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $X$ a Noetherian scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (the field spectrum is Noetherian). Thus $X$ has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], and they cover $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. For each $C_i$, the complement in $C_i$ of the union of the other components is a nonempty open subset: it is open because there are finitely many components, and nonempty because an irreducible component is not contained in the finite union of the other maximal irreducible closed subsets.

source.place: Tags 01T6 and 0BA8, together with Topology Tag 004W, as used in the proof of Varieties Tag 0AYY

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] applied to $X$, the underlying space of $X$ has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most 1. Assume that $Z$ contains a strict chain $W_0\subsetneq W_1$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets (with the subspace topology). Since $Z$ is closed in $X$, these are also irreducible closed subsets of $X$. By the component cover, $W_1\subseteq C_i$ for some $i$. If $W_1$ is strictly contained in $C_i$, then $W_0\subsetneq W_1\subsetneq C_i$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $X$ of length 2, contradicting the preceding dimension bound. If $W_1=C_i$, then $C_i\subseteq Z$, so $Z$ contains $U_i=X\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$, which is open in $X$ because the union is finite and closed, and is nonempty by step 1. This contradicts that the underlying set of $Z$ is nowhere dense in $X$: since $Z$ is closed, its interior would contain the nonempty open set $U_i$. Hence no such chain exists, so the underlying space of $Z$ has topological dimension at most zero. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], this is the asserted $\dim Z\le0$.

proof.text: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$, and let $Z\to X$ be a closed immersion with underlying closed subset of dimension at most zero. Applying [lem-sc-dim0-finite] to these explicitly stated hypotheses shows that every point of $Z$ is closed in $Z$ (and also covers the empty case).
